verdict: M8 RESOLVED AFFIRMATIVELY, and with no period matrix. The commutant of the algebra generated by the Hecke operators and the canonical graph coupling V is exactly the scalars. Since the Hodge complex structure J is real, satisfies J^2 = -I, and commutes with every Hecke operator, it cannot commute with V — a real scalar cannot square to -1. Hence [V, J] != 0 unconditionally: the graph channel has a nonvanishing J-antilinear part. Combined with M7 (V commutes with iota*) and the antiholomorphy of iota* (J iota* = -iota* J), the CP-odd content lands entirely in the iota*-ODD sector — the sector M6 identified as carrying the CP charge. The M6/M7 tension is therefore resolvable in principle at ZERO parameter cost, since the Hodge structure is forced by the curve rather than chosen. What remains is quantitative, not structural: the SIZE of the transmitted CP-odd mixing requires the period matrix in the modular- symbol basis, which is now the well-posed successor task.
